eagle-and-jaguar-warriors.s: The Eagle and Jaguar warriors were elite military orders of the Aztec Empire. Membership was earned mainly by capturing enemies in battle, and it brought high status, distinctive costumes and privileges.

early-dynastic-period.s: The Early Dynastic period is the phase of southern Mesopotamian history, roughly the first half of the third millennium BCE, when Sumerian city-states such as Ur, Uruk, Lagash and Kish competed for dominance. It preceded the unification of Mesopotamia by Sargon and the rise of…

early-muslim-conquests.s: The early Muslim conquests were the rapid expansion of the Arab Muslim state in the 7th century, following the death of the Prophet Muhammad. Arab armies overran the Sasanian Empire and took Syria and Egypt from Byzantium, and expansion continued under the Umayyad Caliphate.

east-africa.s: East Africa is the eastern region of the African continent, including the Horn of Africa and the Swahili coast. It was home to the Aksumite Empire and a target of colonial expansion by the Portuguese Empire, the German Empire and the Italian Empire.

east-african-campaign-world-war-ii.s: The East African campaign was a Second World War campaign fought in 1940–1941 between British and Commonwealth forces, with Ethiopian resistance fighters, and the Italian forces in Ethiopia, Eritrea and Italian Somaliland. Its outcome destroyed Italian East Africa, restored…

east-francia.s: East Francia was the eastern kingdom created when the Carolingian Empire was divided by the Treaty of Verdun in 843, initially under Louis the German. Covering much of present-day Germany, it developed into the Kingdom of Germany and became the core of the later Holy Roman…

east-india-company.s: The East India Company was an English, later British, chartered trading company founded in 1600. Beginning as a trading concern, it became a military and governing power in India, defeating the Maratha Empire and the Sikh Empire and reducing the Mughal Empire to a pensioner,…

east-indies.s: The East Indies is a historical term for the islands of South-East Asia, especially the Indonesian archipelago. The Dutch East Indies formed the centre of the Dutch Empire, valued for spices and later plantation crops, until the Empire of Japan occupied them during the Second…

east-timor.s: East Timor (Timor-Leste) is a country occupying the eastern half of the island of Timor in South-East Asia. It was a Portuguese colony for centuries and one of the last remnants of the Portuguese Empire; after Portugal withdrew in 1975 it was occupied by Indonesia and became…

eastern-europe.s: Eastern Europe is the eastern part of the European continent, including the plains between the Baltic, the Black Sea and the Urals. The Khazar Khaganate dominated much of its south-eastern steppe and trade routes, while the Mongol Empire conquered the Rus' principalities and…

eastern-orthodox-church.s: The Eastern Orthodox Church is the body of Christian churches that follow the Byzantine tradition and recognise the authority of the ecumenical councils, separating from Rome in the Middle Ages. It was the state church of the Byzantine Empire and later of the Russian Empire,…

eastern-turkestan.s: Eastern Turkestan is a historical name for the Tarim Basin and surrounding lands, roughly corresponding to southern Xinjiang in north-western China. The Qing Empire conquered the region in the eighteenth century after defeating the Dzungars, and it later reasserted control…

eastern-turkic-khaganate.s: The Eastern Turkic Khaganate was the eastern half of the Gokturk realm after it split into eastern and western branches in the late sixth century. Based in Mongolia, it was a major power on China's northern frontier until the Tang Dynasty under Emperor Taizong defeated it in…

ebarat-ii.s: Ebarat II was an Elamite ruler of around 1900 BCE. According to the account, he established the sukkalmah system, a tripartite governing hierarchy that is regarded as the most sophisticated constitutional innovation of the Elamite Confederation.

ebla.s: Ebla was an ancient city in northern Syria that flourished in the third millennium BCE and is famous for its large archive of cuneiform tablets. It fell to the Akkadian Empire during the campaigns of Sargon or Naram-Sin, whose conquests extended Akkadian reach to its greatest…

ebony.s: Ebony is a dense, dark hardwood from tropical Africa that was highly valued as a luxury material in the ancient world. It was among the goods that moved from the African interior to Egypt, appearing in the trade of the Egyptian Empire New Kingdom, including Hatshepsut's…

ebro-river.s: The Ebro is a major river of north-eastern Spain, flowing into the Mediterranean. At its height the Almoravid Empire stretched from the Senegal River in West Africa to the Ebro, marking the northern limit of its territory in al-Andalus.

ecbatana.s: Ecbatana, modern Hamadan in western Iran, was the capital of the Median Empire. After Cyrus the Great conquered Media, it became one of the royal residences and administrative centres of the Achaemenid Empire, used especially as a summer capital.

ecological-warfare.s: Ecological warfare refers to military methods that target an enemy's environment and resources, such as water supplies or farmland. Hammurabi of the Babylonian Empire is credited with this approach, destroying Eshnunna around 1755 BCE by damming its water supply instead of…

edict-of-milan.s: The Edict of Milan was the agreement of 313 CE between the emperors Constantine and Licinius granting religious toleration throughout the Roman Empire, including to Christians. It ended official persecution and opened the way to the rise of Christianity as the empire's…

edict-of-telipinu.s: The Edict of Telipinu is a Hittite text issued by King Telipinu around 1525 BCE. It recounts earlier periods of royal murder and instability and establishes rules of succession to the throne, along with procedures for punishing crimes within the royal family.

edicts-of-ashoka.s: The Edicts of Ashoka are a series of inscriptions on rocks and pillars issued by the Maurya emperor Ashoka in the third century BCE. They proclaim his commitment to dharma, his remorse after the Kalinga war, and policies of tolerance, welfare and moral government.

edirne.s: Edirne, the ancient Adrianople, is a city in European Turkey near the Greek and Bulgarian borders. It served as the capital of the Ottoman Empire before the conquest of Constantinople in 1453, and it is home to the Selimiye Mosque, regarded as a masterpiece of the architect…

edo-tokyo.s: Edo, renamed Tokyo in 1868, was the seat of the Tokugawa Shogunate. Tokugawa Ieyasu made it his base, and it grew into one of the largest cities in the world, partly because the alternate attendance system required daimyo to spend time there.

edo-bay.s: Edo Bay, now Tokyo Bay, is the bay on which Edo stands. In 1853 Commodore Matthew Perry's 'Black Ships' entered it and demanded that Japan open to American trade, exposing the military weakness of the Tokugawa Shogunate and setting in motion the events that led to its fall.

edo-people.s: The Edo people, also called the Bini, are an ethnic group of southern Nigeria. They founded and formed the core population of the Benin Empire, whose capital, Benin City, and Oba institution remain central to Edo identity, along with the celebrated Benin bronzes.

edo-period.s: The Edo period is the era of Japanese history from 1603 to 1868 under the rule of the Tokugawa Shogunate, named after its capital Edo. It was a long period of internal peace, restricted foreign contact, urban growth and cultural flourishing, during which the samurai became…

edward-ullendorff.s: Edward Ullendorff was a British scholar of Semitic languages and Ethiopian studies. Accounts of the Ethiopian Empire cite his judgement that Emperor Zara Yaqob was the greatest Ethiopian ruler since the Aksumite era.

egon-schiele.s: Egon Schiele was an Austrian expressionist painter active in Vienna in the early twentieth century, known for his intense figure drawings and portraits. He is cited, alongside Klimt and Kokoschka, as part of the cultural flowering of Vienna in the late Austro-Hungarian Empire.

egypt.s: Egypt is a country in north-eastern Africa centred on the Nile valley, one of the oldest centres of civilisation. Its wealth and position made it a prize for many empires: it was the core of the Egyptian Empire New Kingdom and the Ptolemaic Empire, and was ruled by the…

egyptian-conquest-of-kordofan.s: The Egyptian conquest of Kordofan in 1821 was part of the expansion of Muhammad Ali's Egypt into Sudan. It removed Kordofan from the Darfur Sultanate, severing its eastern trade connections and diverting Nile valley commerce, which led to a long economic decline that weakened…

egyptian-hieroglyphs.s: Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system of ancient Egypt, using pictorial signs for sounds and words. The peace treaty between the Hittite Empire and Egypt after Kadesh survives both in Akkadian cuneiform at Hattusa and in hieroglyphs at Karnak, illustrating the…

egyptians.s: The Egyptians are the people of the Nile valley in north-eastern Africa. In antiquity they formed the population of the Egyptian Empire New Kingdom, served as soldiers and subjects under the Achaemenid Empire, and under the Ptolemaic Empire were recruited into the army,…

ehengbuda.s: Ehengbuda was an Oba of Benin who died in 1606. He is regarded as the last of the great warrior kings who, from Ewuare onward, combined military expansion with artistic patronage.

eight-banners.s: The Eight Banners were the military and administrative organisation created by the Manchu leader Nurhaci around 1601. All Manchu households were enrolled in banners, later joined by Mongol and Han banners.

eighteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.s: The Eighteenth Dynasty was the ruling house of Egypt that founded the New Kingdom after the expulsion of the Hyksos. Its rulers, including Ahmose I, Hatshepsut, Thutmose III, Akhenaten and Tutankhamun, built the Egyptian Empire New Kingdom, extending Egyptian power into the…

einhard.s: Einhard was a Frankish scholar and courtier at the court of Charlemagne. He wrote the Life of Charlemagne, a biography that is one of the most important sources for the reign of the emperor and for the government of the Carolingian Empire.

ejisu.s: Ejisu is a town in the Ashanti region of present-day Ghana. Its queen mother, Yaa Asantewaa, led the War of the Golden Stool against the British in 1900, the last major armed resistance of the Ashanti Empire against colonial rule.

el-fasher.s: El Fasher is a city in western Sudan that became the capital of the Darfur Sultanate. From there the sultan governed through a hierarchy of territorial title-holders, and the city was again the seat of the restored sultanate under Ali Dinar.

el-hadj-umar-tall.s: El Hadj Umar Tall was a West African Muslim scholar and military leader of the nineteenth century who founded the Toucouleur state through conquests in the 1850s and 1860s. Accounts of the Sokoto Caliphate identify him among the jihad leaders who drew inspiration from Sokoto's…

elam.s: Elam was an ancient region in south-western Iran, centred on Susa and the highlands of Anshan. Its rulers were long-standing rivals of Mesopotamian states, clashing with the Akkadian Empire, the Babylonian Empire and the Assyrian Empire.

elamite-confederation.s: The Elamite Confederation refers to the states of ancient Elam in south-western Iran, which endured for more than two thousand years. Elam fought repeatedly with Mesopotamian powers, sacking Ur and ending the Neo-Sumerian Empire, conquering Babylon around 1158 BCE, and finally…

elamite-conquest-of-babylon-c-1158-bce.s: The Elamite conquest of Babylon around 1158 BCE was a campaign by Elamite kings, notably Shutruk-Nahhunte and his successors, which brought an end to the Kassite dynasty. The Elamites carried off monuments to Susa, including the Code of Hammurabi stele, and the episode marked…

elamite-language.s: Elamite is the extinct language of ancient Elam, written first in its own scripts and later in cuneiform. It has no known relatives.

elamite-sack-of-ur.s: The Elamite sack of Ur took place around 2004 BCE, when Elamite forces captured the city of Ur and took its last king, Ibbi-Sin, captive. It brought an end to the Neo-Sumerian Empire and was later lamented in Sumerian literature.

elamites.s: The Elamites were the people of ancient Elam in south-western Iran, who formed the Elamite Confederation. They were long-term rivals and neighbours of Mesopotamian states, contributing to the fall of the Neo-Sumerian Empire and fighting the Assyrian Empire.

elective-monarchy.s: An elective monarchy is a system in which the monarch is chosen by election rather than inheriting the throne. In the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth the whole nobility could take part in electing the king, who had to accept conditions limiting his powers.

el-ghaba.s: El-Ghaba was the royal town of Koumbi Saleh, the capital of the Ghana Empire. Described by Arab writers, it contained the king's stone-walled palace and a sacred grove, and stood some distance from the separate Muslim merchants' town.

elmina.s: Elmina is a town on the coast of present-day Ghana, site of São Jorge da Mina, the castle built by the Portuguese in 1482. Later taken by the Dutch, it was a major centre of the gold and slave trades, and its trade relations, including the Dutch connection, mattered to the…

emancipation-reform-of-1861.s: The emancipation reform of 1861 was the decree of Tsar Alexander II abolishing serfdom in the Russian Empire. It freed millions of peasants, though they had to pay redemption for land, and it opened a period of wider reforms in local government, the courts and the army.

emir.s: An emir is an Arabic title meaning commander or prince, used for military leaders, governors and rulers in Islamic states. In the Mamluk Sultanate emirs were the senior military officers, in the Ilkhanate powerful emirs dominated late politics, and in the Sokoto Caliphate…

emirate.s: An emirate is a territory ruled by an emir. Under the Abbasid Caliphate many provinces became effectively autonomous emirates, and the Umayyad survivors in Spain founded the Emirate of Córdoba.

emirate-of-cordoba.s: The Emirate of Córdoba was the Muslim state in Iberia founded in 756 by Abd al-Rahman I, a survivor of the Umayyad dynasty after its overthrow by the Abbasids. It preserved Umayyad rule in al-Andalus and was proclaimed a caliphate in 929, continuing the legacy of the Umayyad…

emperor-gaozu-of-tang.s: Emperor Gaozu, born Li Yuan, was the founder of the Tang Dynasty. A Sui general, he rebelled during the collapse of the Sui and founded the dynasty in 618 CE.

emperor-huizong.s: Emperor Huizong was a Northern Song emperor, celebrated as a painter, calligrapher and patron of the arts but criticised for political neglect. When the Jurchen Jin captured Kaifeng in 1127, he and his son were taken captive, ending the Northern Song and forcing the Song…

emperor-meiji.s: Emperor Meiji was emperor of Japan from 1867 to 1912. The Meiji Restoration of 1868 ended the Tokugawa Shogunate and restored imperial rule in his name, and his reign saw rapid modernisation, industrialisation and the building of the Empire of Japan into a major power.

emperor-shenzong-of-song.s: Emperor Shenzong was an emperor of the Northern Song in the late eleventh century. He backed the reforms of Wang Anshi, the New Policies, which aimed to strengthen state finances and the military of the Song Dynasty but provoked intense factional opposition.

emperor-taizong-of-song.s: Emperor Taizong was the second emperor of the Song Dynasty, succeeding his brother Taizu. He completed the reunification of China by conquering the remaining southern states and Northern Han, but his campaigns against the Liao failed to recover the northern frontier regions.

emperor-taizong-of-tang.s: Emperor Taizong, born Li Shimin, was the second emperor of the Tang Dynasty (r. 626–649).

emperor-taizu-of-song.s: Emperor Taizu, born Zhao Kuangyin, was the founder of the Song Dynasty. A military commander, he seized power in 960 and began reunifying China.

emperor-wu-of-han.s: Emperor Wu was the seventh emperor of the Han Dynasty (r. 141–87 BCE).

emperor-xuanzong-of-tang.s: Emperor Xuanzong was an emperor of the Tang Dynasty (r. 713–741) whose era is remembered as a cultural and political high point.

emperor-yang-of-sui.s: Emperor Yang was the second emperor of the Sui dynasty. He undertook vast projects, including the completion of the Grand Canal, and launched costly failed campaigns against the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

empire-of-japan.s: The Empire of Japan was the Japanese state from the Meiji Restoration of 1868 until the post-war constitution of 1947. It modernised rapidly, defeated China and Russia, acquired colonies including Taiwan and Korea, and expanded across East and South-East Asia before its defeat…

empire-on-which-the-sun-never-sets.n: Empire on which the sun never sets
empire-on-which-the-sun-never-sets.s: The 'empire on which the sun never sets' is a phrase describing an empire so extensive that some part of it is always in daylight. It was first applied to the Spanish Empire under the Habsburgs, especially after the union with Portugal in 1580, when its possessions spanned…

empress-dowager-cixi.s: Empress Dowager Cixi was the dominant figure at the Qing court from the 1860s until her death in 1908, ruling as regent for the Tongzhi and Guangxu emperors. She supported some limited modernisation but suppressed the Hundred Days' Reform of 1898 and backed the Boxers in 1900.

encomienda.s: The encomienda was a system in the Spanish Empire by which the crown granted colonists the right to extract labour and tribute from groups of indigenous people, in return for protecting them and instructing them in Christianity. In practice it led to severe abuse, prompting…

end-of-kanem-bornu-independence.s: The end of Kanem–Bornu independence came in 1893, when the Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr conquered Bornu. His rule was short-lived, as the region was soon divided among the British, French and Germans, bringing to a close the long history of the Kanem-Bornu Empire as an…

endubis.s: Endubis was a king of Aksum who reigned around 270 CE. He is the first Aksumite ruler known to have issued coins, in gold, silver and bronze, making the Aksumite Empire one of the first African states outside Roman control to mint its own currency.

england.s: England is a country in the south of Great Britain. A rising maritime and commercial power from the sixteenth century, it united with Scotland in 1707 to form Great Britain and became the core of the British Empire.

english-language.s: English is a Germanic language that originated in England. Spread across the world by the British Empire through settlement, administration, education and trade, it became the language of government and elites in many colonies and is now one of the most widely spoken…

enheduanna.s: Enheduanna was the daughter of Sargon of Akkad, appointed high priestess of the moon god Nanna at Ur. She is known as the author of hymns to the goddess Inanna and is often called the first named author in history.

enmebaragesi.s: Enmebaragesi was a king of Kish who lived around 2700 BCE and is one of the earliest Mesopotamian rulers attested in inscriptions. The Sumerian King List records that he defeated the Elamites, among the earliest recorded conflicts in the history of the Elamite Confederation.

ensi.s: Ensi was a Sumerian title for the ruler or governor of a city-state. Under the Akkadian Empire, the ensis of conquered cities were brought under royal control and often replaced by loyal Akkadian appointees, turning them into provincial governors within a centralised empire.

entrepot.s: An entrepôt is a port or trading centre where goods are imported, stored and re-exported, often without further processing. Control of such hubs gave states wealth and influence; examples include Adulis for the Aksumite Empire, Zeila for the Adal Sultanate, Palembang and the…

environmental-degradation.s: Environmental degradation refers to the long-term damage of land, soil, water and forests through overuse, salinisation or deforestation, often combined with climatic change. It undermined the economic base of several states, including salinisation of fields in the…

ephor.s: Ephor was the title of senior magistrates, best known from Sparta, who supervised the conduct of kings and officials. Greek writers, notably Aristotle, compared certain Carthaginian institutions to the Spartan ephors when describing the constitution of the Punic Empire.

epic-of-gilgamesh.s: The Epic of Gilgamesh is an ancient Mesopotamian poem about the legendary king of Uruk and his search for immortality. It is one of the oldest surviving works of literature.

epidemic-disease.s: Epidemic disease refers to outbreaks of infectious illness that killed large parts of a population, disrupting economies, armies and government. The Black Death struck the Mamluk Sultanate, the Ilkhanate and the Yuan Dynasty, while smallpox and other diseases introduced by…

equal-field-system.s: The equal-field system was a land allocation system used in China from the Northern Wei to the Tang Dynasty. The state allocated land to households according to their size and labour, linking land to tax and labour obligations.

equites.s: The equites, or equestrian order, were the second rank of the Roman aristocracy below the senators. Originally Rome's cavalry, they became a wealthy class of businessmen and, under the Roman Empire, filled important administrative posts such as prefect of Egypt.

erekle-ii.s: Erekle II was a Georgian king of the eighteenth century who served in Nader Shah's campaigns. After Nader's assassination in 1747 and the collapse of the Afsharid Empire, he asserted Georgian independence, later uniting eastern Georgia and placing it under Russian protection…

eresoyen.s: Eresoyen was an Oba of Benin in the first half of the eighteenth century. Following the near-collapse of the monarchy in the Ewuakpe civil war, his reign, along with that of Akenzua I, brought a partial recovery that stabilised the core territories of the Benin Empire.

eritrea.s: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea coast. The Aksumite Empire's port of Adulis lay there, and from the late nineteenth century it became Italy's first colony and a base for the Italian Empire's invasion of Ethiopia.

esagila.s: The Esagila was the great temple of Marduk in Babylon, the most important sanctuary of the city. The rulers of the Chaldean Empire, especially Nebuchadnezzar II, lavishly restored it, together with the nearby ziggurat Etemenanki, as part of their rebuilding of Babylon.

esarhaddon.s: Esarhaddon was king of the Assyrian Empire in the seventh century BCE, the son of Sennacherib and father of Ashurbanipal. He rebuilt Babylon and in 671 BCE invaded Egypt, driving out the Kushite pharaoh Taharqa and capturing Memphis, a defeat that began the Kushite Empire's…

eshnunna.s: Eshnunna was an ancient city-state in the Diyala valley, east of the Tigris, known for its law code. It was a rival of Babylon and was finally destroyed by Hammurabi of the Babylonian Empire around 1755 BCE.

esigie.s: Esigie was an Oba of Benin who ruled during 1504–1550. He defeated the Igala and enlarged the Benin Empire, developed relations with the Portuguese, including trade and Christian missions, and his mother Idia became the first Iyoba (queen mother).

eso.s: The Eso were an elite corps of cavalry commanders in the Oyo Empire, traditionally numbering seventy, serving as the Alaafin's personal military instrument. They formed the organisational core of Oyo's cavalry army, which was central to the empire's expansion.

estado-da-india.s: The Estado da Índia was the Portuguese administration of its possessions in Asia and East Africa, headed by a viceroy or governor based at Goa from 1530. It coordinated the Portuguese Empire's network of fortified trading posts, and its intervention in the Horn of Africa,…

estado-novo-portugal.s: The Estado Novo ('New State') was the authoritarian regime that ruled Portugal from 1933 to 1974, led for most of that time by António de Oliveira Salazar. It insisted on keeping the colonies of the Portuguese Empire and fought costly colonial wars in Africa, until the…

estonia.s: Estonia is a country on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea. Northern Estonia came under Swedish rule in 1561, making it one of the first Baltic provinces of the Swedish Empire.

ethiopia.s: Ethiopia is a country in the Horn of Africa with one of the longest continuous state traditions in the world. It was the home of the Aksumite Empire and its successor, the Ethiopian Empire, fought a long war with the Adal Sultanate, and defeated Italy at Adwa in 1896 before…

ethiopian-empire.s: The Ethiopian Empire was the Christian monarchy of the Ethiopian highlands that lasted from the restoration of the Solomonic dynasty in 1270 until the deposition of Haile Selassie in 1974. It survived the Adal invasion in the sixteenth century, defeated Italy at Adwa in 1896…

ethiopian-highlands.s: The Ethiopian highlands are a large mountainous plateau in the Horn of Africa. Their fertile land and natural defences made them the heartland of the Aksumite Empire and its Christian successors, and their invasion by the Adal Sultanate in the sixteenth century came close to…

ethiopian-orthodox-church.s: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church is the ancient Christian church of Ethiopia, belonging to the Oriental Orthodox communion. It was founded after the conversion of the Aksumite Empire under King Ezana in the fourth century and became a pillar of the Ethiopian Empire,…

ethiopian-adal-war.s: The Ethiopian–Adal War was a conflict fought in 1527–1543 between the Adal Sultanate, led by Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi, and the Christian Ethiopian Empire. Adal forces overran most of the highlands, but Portuguese intervention and Ahmad's death at the Battle of Wayna Daga in…

ethnic-hierarchy-and-discrimination.s: Ethnic hierarchy and discrimination refers to the formal or informal ranking of subjects by ethnicity or origin, which alienated large parts of an empire's population. The Yuan Dynasty divided its subjects into ranked classes with Chinese at the bottom, the Umayyad Caliphate…

ethnological-museum-berlin.s: The Ethnological Museum of Berlin is one of the largest museums of non-European art and cultures. It holds a major collection of Benin Bronzes looted from the Benin Empire by the British in 1897, and it has been a significant participant in the debate over restitution of these…

euclid.s: Euclid was a Greek mathematician of Alexandria, active around 300 BCE, whose Elements became the foundational textbook of geometry. His work was translated into Arabic during the translation movement of the Abbasid Caliphate, preserving and transmitting it to later Islamic and…

eumenes-ii.s: Eumenes II was king of Pergamon in the early second century BCE and an ally of Rome. His cavalry supported the Roman army at the Battle of Magnesia in 190 BCE, which inflicted a heavy defeat on the Seleucid Empire, and Pergamon received much of Seleucid Asia Minor afterwards.

eunuch.s: A eunuch is a castrated man, and in many courts eunuchs served as palace officials, guards of the royal household and administrators. Being unable to found dynasties, they were often trusted by rulers.

euphrates.s: The Euphrates is one of the two great rivers of Mesopotamia, flowing from Anatolia through Syria and Iraq to the Persian Gulf. Its waters supported the irrigation agriculture of the Akkadian Empire, the Neo-Sumerian Empire, the Babylonian Empire and the Chaldean Empire, and it…

eurasia.s: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia. Its steppe belt and trade routes linked empires across vast distances, enabling the expansion of nomadic powers such as the Xiongnu Empire and the Mongol Empire, and the exchange of goods and ideas through empires such as…

europe.s: Europe is the western part of the Eurasian landmass. It was the home of empires such as the Roman, Carolingian, Holy Roman and Austro-Hungarian, and from the fifteenth century European states built overseas empires that reached the Americas, Africa and Asia.

european-colonial-expansion.s: European colonial expansion describes the growth of European empires overseas from the fifteenth to the twentieth century, through trade, conquest and settlement. It undermined or destroyed many states, as in the British conquest of the Mughal Empire and Maratha Empire, French…

european-union.s: The European Union is a political and economic union of European states, developed from the European communities founded in the 1950s. Charlemagne and the Carolingian Empire, which united much of western Europe, are often invoked as symbolic forerunners of European unity in…

eusebio-de-queiros-law.s: The Eusébio de Queirós Law was a Brazilian law of 1850, named after the minister of justice who sponsored it, which effectively ended the transatlantic slave trade to the Brazilian Empire. Passed under heavy British pressure, it was an important step on the road towards the…

evian-accords.s: The Évian Accords were the agreements signed in 1962 between France and the Algerian National Liberation Front, ending the Algerian War. They led to Algeria's independence that year and marked one of the final chapters in the dismantling of the French Empire.

ewedo.s: Ewedo was an Oba of Benin who ruled c. 1260–1274.

eweka-i.s: Eweka I is the legendary first Oba of Benin, traditionally installed around 1180 CE after the Ogiso dynasty lost legitimacy. Tradition links him to Ife through his father Oranmiyan.

ewuakpe.s: Ewuakpe was an Oba of Benin whose reign, c. 1700–1712, saw a civil war that brought the Benin Empire close to collapse.

ewuare-the-great.s: Ewuare the Great was an Oba of Benin (r. 1440–1473) who transformed the kingdom into an empire.

execution-of-the-mongol-envoys-1218.s: The execution of the Mongol envoys in 1218 followed the massacre of a Mongol-sponsored trade caravan at Otrar. When Genghis Khan sent envoys to demand redress, Shah Muhammad II of the Khwarazmian Empire had them killed or humiliated.

expressionism.s: Expressionism was a modernist movement in art, literature and music in the early twentieth century that sought to express emotional experience rather than physical reality. In Vienna it flourished in the work of painters such as Egon Schiele and Oskar Kokoschka, forming part…

expulsion-of-the-jews-from-spain.n: Expulsion of the Jews from Spain
expulsion-of-the-jews-from-spain.s: The expulsion of the Jews from Spain was ordered by Ferdinand and Isabella in 1492, forcing Jews to convert or leave. Many of the exiles found refuge in the Ottoman Empire, where they settled in cities such as Istanbul and Thessaloniki and contributed to commerce, medicine and…

extraterritoriality.s: Extraterritoriality is the exemption of foreigners from the jurisdiction of local courts, so that they are tried under their own country's law. Imposed on the Qing Empire by the unequal treaties after the Opium Wars, it became a symbol of foreign encroachment on Chinese…

extremadura.s: Extremadura is a region of western Spain bordering Portugal. After the Almohad victory at Alarcos in 1195, Almohad Caliphate forces devastated Extremadura and neighbouring regions, raiding deep into Christian territory.

eyes-and-ears-of-the-king.n: Eyes and Ears of the King
eyes-and-ears-of-the-king.s: The 'Eyes and Ears of the King' were officials of the Achaemenid Empire who, according to Greek sources, acted as royal inspectors and informants. They reported to the king on the conduct of satraps and the state of the provinces, serving as a check on provincial power.

ezana.s: Ezana was a king of Aksum who reigned c. 325–340 CE.

ezana-stone.s: The Ezana Stone is an inscribed stela at Aksum recording the deeds of King Ezana in the fourth century CE. Written in Ge'ez, Sabaean and Greek, it commemorates his military campaigns and reflects his conversion to Christianity.

ernest-augustus-elector-of-hanover.s: Ernest Augustus, Elector of Hanover, was a prince of the house of Brunswick-Lüneburg who was Lutheran Prince-Bishop of Osnabrück from 1662 and Duke of Calenberg from 1679. He centralised his state, employed Leibniz, and in 1692 won from Emperor Leopold I the rank of ninth…

ernest-augustus-i-duke-of-saxe-weimar-ei.n: Ernest Augustus I, Duke of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach
ernest-augustus-i-duke-of-saxe-weimar-ei.s: Ernest Augustus I was Duke of Saxe-Weimar from 1728. When the ducal line of Saxe-Eisenach died out in 1741 he inherited its lands, creating the united Duchy of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach.

ernest-augustus-king-of-hanover.s: Ernest Augustus, King of Hanover, was the fifth son of George III and Duke of Cumberland. When Victoria became British queen in 1837, Hanover's Salic law barred her, ending the personal union, and he became king.

ernest-augustus-duke-of-brunswick.s: Ernest Augustus, Duke of Brunswick, was a grandson of the last King of Hanover. His marriage in 1913 to Victoria Louise, daughter of Kaiser Wilhelm II, reconciled the Hanoverian Welfs with the Hohenzollerns and allowed him to take the throne of Brunswick, held by regents since…

emperor-wu-of-liu-song.s: Emperor Wu of Liu Song, born Liu Yu, was a general of humble origins who rose to dominate the Eastern Jin court. He overthrew the usurper Huan Xuan in 404, conquered Southern Yan in 410, Western Shu in 413 and Later Qin with Chang'an in 417.

eastern-states-agency.s: The Eastern States Agency was a political agency of British India formed in 1933 to supervise the princely states of Orissa, Chhattisgarh and Chota Nagpur in eastern India, about forty states in all. It took over the work of the Orissa and Chhattisgarh state superintendents.

el-cid.s: El Cid, Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, was a Castilian nobleman and soldier. Exiled by Alfonso VI, he served the Muslim rulers of the taifa of Zaragoza and collected tribute from other taifas in eastern al-Andalus.

emilio-aguinaldo.s: Emilio Aguinaldo was a leader of the Philippine Revolution against Spain from 1896. After the Pact of Biak-na-Bato he went into exile, returned in 1898 during the Spanish–American War and declared independence on 12 June 1898.

european-economic-community.s: The European Economic Community was a customs union and common market founded by the Treaty of Rome in 1957 by France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. It abolished internal tariffs, created a common agricultural policy and drew in new members,…

emperor-wen-of-han.s: Emperor Wen of Han, born Liu Heng, was a son of Liu Bang who was made King of Dai before being chosen emperor in 180 BCE after the fall of the Lü clan. His reign, to 157 BCE, was remembered as a model of frugal and lenient government: he lowered taxes, abolished mutilating…

emperor-wen-of-liu-song.s: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, born Liu Yilong, was a son of the dynasty's founder Liu Yu and reigned from 424 to 453. His Yuanjia era brought prosperity and cultural achievement to the southern court at Jiankang, though his campaigns against the Northern Wei failed.

emperor-wen-of-sui.s: Emperor Wen of Sui, born Yang Jian, was a Northern Zhou official who seized power and founded the Sui dynasty in 581. He conquered the southern Chen dynasty in 589, reuniting China after nearly three centuries of division.

entre-rios-province.s: Entre Ríos is a province of Argentina between the Paraná and Uruguay rivers. In the independence era its caudillos joined Artigas's Federal League, and in 1820 Francisco Ramírez proclaimed the short-lived Republic of Entre Ríos.

ernest-ii-duke-of-saxe-gotha-altenburg.s: Ernest II was Duke of Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg from 1772 and an Enlightenment ruler. A patron of science, he founded the Seeberg observatory near Gotha, which became a leading centre of astronomy under Franz Xaver von Zach.

ernst-ii-duke-of-saxe-altenburg.s: Ernst II was the last Duke of Saxe-Altenburg, reigning from 1908. He served as a general in the First World War.

ernest-ii-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha.n: Ernest II, Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
ernest-ii-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha.s: Ernest II was Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha from 1844 and the elder brother of Prince Albert, husband of Queen Victoria. A liberal and supporter of German unification, he backed the German national movement and sided with Prussia in 1866.

ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-gotha.s: Ernest I, called the Pious, founded the Duchy of Saxe-Gotha in 1640. After the Thirty Years' War he rebuilt his lands as a model Lutheran state, introducing compulsory schooling and orderly administration from Friedenstein Castle in Gotha.

ezzelino-iii-da-romano.s: Ezzelino III da Romano was a Ghibelline lord of the March of Treviso and an ally of Emperor Frederick II. From the 1220s to the 1250s he dominated Verona, Vicenza and Padua, ruling with a cruelty that made him a byword for tyranny.

east-germany.s: East Germany, the German Democratic Republic, was the communist state formed in October 1949 from the Soviet occupation zone of Germany. Ruled by the Socialist Unity Party, it abolished the historic Länder in 1952 and built the Berlin Wall in 1961.

eamon-de-valera.s: Éamon de Valera was a leader of Irish independence and a commander in the Easter Rising of 1916. He was president of the revolutionary Irish Republic from 1919 and opposed the Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921.

east-frisia.s: East Frisia is a coastal region of north-western Germany between the Dollart and the Jade, including the East Frisian Islands. In the Middle Ages it was part of the Frisian Freedom, governed by local chieftains, until the Cirksena family united it as an imperial county in 1464.

eleanor-of-aquitaine.s: Eleanor of Aquitaine was Duchess of Aquitaine and Countess of Poitou in her own right from 1137. She was queen of France as wife of Louis VII, and after the annulment of that marriage she married Henry of Anjou in 1152, bringing Aquitaine into the Angevin Empire.

elector-palatine.s: Elector Palatine was the title of the Count Palatine of the Rhine as one of the prince-electors of the Holy Roman Empire, confirmed by the Golden Bull of 1356. The office was held by the Wittelsbach family, ruling from Heidelberg, and passed between its branches such as…

estonian-war-of-independence.s: The Estonian War of Independence was fought by the new Republic of Estonia against Soviet Russia and then the Baltic German Landeswehr. With British naval support and Finnish volunteers, Estonian forces drove out the Red Army in early 1919 and defeated the Landeswehr at Cēsis…

ernest-duke-of-bavaria.s: Ernest was Duke of Bavaria-Munich from 1397 until his death in 1438, ruling at first with his brother William III. He defended Munich against his cousins of Bavaria-Ingolstadt.

ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha.n: Ernest I, Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha.s: Ernest I was Duke of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld from 1806 and, after the Ernestine redistribution of 1826, the first Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha. He gained the Rhineland Principality of Lichtenberg in 1816 but sold it to Prussia in 1834.

ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-altenburg.s: Ernest I was Duke of Saxe-Altenburg from 1853 until his death in 1908. A Prussian general, he led his small Thuringian duchy into the North German Confederation in 1867 and the German Empire in 1871, and fought in the Franco-Prussian War.

early-bronze-age.s: The Early Bronze Age is the first phase of the Bronze Age in the Near East and the Aegean, roughly 3300 to 2000 BCE. In the Levant it saw the first walled towns, such as Megiddo; in Greece, sites like Tiryns and Orchomenos grew into substantial settlements with large central…

east-punjab.s: East Punjab was the Indian province formed from the eastern part of British Punjab after the partition of 1947. Small princely states and estates in the region were absorbed into it.

easter-ross.s: Easter Ross is the eastern lowland part of Ross in the northern Scottish Highlands, between the Cromarty and Dornoch Firths. Ptolemy placed the Decantae there.

eastern-ganga-dynasty.s: The Eastern Ganga dynasty ruled Kalinga, modern Odisha, in eastern India. Its imperial phase began under Anantavarman Chodaganga, who conquered the Somavamshi lands around 1110 and began the Jagannath Temple at Puri.

eduard-shevardnadze.s: Eduard Shevardnadze was First Secretary of the Communist Party of the Georgian SSR from 1972 to 1985 and Soviet foreign minister under Gorbachev from 1985 to 1990, helping to end the Cold War. He returned to lead independent Georgia in 1992 amid civil war and was president…

edward-the-elder.s: Edward the Elder was King of the Anglo-Saxons from 899 to 924, son of Alfred the Great. With his sister Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, he conquered the Danish-held lands of the southern Danelaw, taking East Anglia and the Five Boroughs in 917–918, and built fortified burhs.

eleftherios-venizelos.s: Eleftherios Venizelos was a Cretan politician who led the campaign for Crete's union with Greece and became Prime Minister of Greece in 1910. He doubled the country's territory in the Balkan Wars.

emerald-buddha.s: The Emerald Buddha is a small statue of the seated Buddha carved from green jade, the palladium of Thailand. Kept for centuries in Lan Na, it was taken to Luang Prabang and then Vientiane in the 16th century.

enele-maafu.s: Enele Maʻafu was a Tongan prince who went to Fiji in the 1840s to look after Tongan interests and built up power in the Lau Islands and eastern Fiji. He formed the Tovata confederacy and was the chief rival of Seru Cakobau.

eric-of-pomerania.s: Eric of Pomerania, a Pomeranian duke's son and great-nephew of Margaret I, was crowned king of Denmark, Norway and Sweden at Kalmar in 1397, the first ruler of the Kalmar Union. He introduced the Sound Toll and fought the counts of Holstein.

eric-williams.s: Eric Williams was a historian and the first Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago, leading the country from 1956 until his death in 1981. His book Capitalism and Slavery argued that economic motives drove British abolition.

errol-barrow.s: Errol Barrow was a Barbadian politician who founded the Democratic Labour Party and became premier of Barbados in 1961. He led the island to independence in 1966 and served as its first Prime Minister until 1976, expanding free education and social welfare.

estanislao-lopez.s: Estanislao López was governor of Santa Fe in the Argentine Littoral from 1818 until his death and one of the leading Federalist caudillos. An ally of José Gervasio Artigas in the Federal League, he made peace with Buenos Aires in the Treaty of Pilar in 1820, then fought his…

eugene-de-beauharnais.s: Eugène de Beauharnais was the son of Joséphine and the adopted stepson of Napoleon. As viceroy he governed the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy from Milan between 1805 and 1814 and commanded armies in the campaigns of 1809 and 1812.

eustace-grenier.s: Eustace Grenier was a knight from northern France who became one of the great barons of the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem. King Baldwin I granted him Sidon after its surrender in 1110, and he also held Caesarea from about the same time; his descendants kept both lordships for…

eight-deer-jaguar-claw.s: Eight Deer Jaguar Claw was a Mixtec ruler whose life is told in pictorial manuscripts such as the Codex Zouche-Nuttall. Born into a noble family linked to Tilantongo, he established himself at Tututepec on the coast around 1083 and then won Tilantongo, uniting much of the…

emperor-wu-of-chen.s: Emperor Wu of Chen, born Chen Baxian, was a Liang general who suppressed the rising of Lý Bí in northern Vietnam in 545 and helped defeat the rebel Hou Jing. Taking control of Jiankang, he deposed the last Liang emperor in 557 and founded the Chen dynasty, the last of the…

english-council-of-state.s: The English Council of State was the executive body of the English republic, set up by the Rump Parliament in February 1649 after the execution of Charles I. It directed foreign policy, the navy and internal security.

early-classic-period.s: The Early Classic period is the first part of the Classic era of Maya civilisation, from about 250 to 600 CE. It saw the spread of dated stone monuments and royal dynasties across the lowlands, the growth of cities such as Tikal, Calakmul and Caracol, and strong influence from…

east-prussia.s: East Prussia was the easternmost part of Prussia on the south-eastern Baltic coast, centred on Königsberg. It grew from the lands of the Teutonic Order left after 1466, which became the Duchy of Prussia in 1525 and the core of the later Kingdom of Prussia.

east-sumatra.s: East Sumatra is the coastal plain of north-eastern Sumatra around Medan, home of Malay sultanates such as Deli, Langkat, Asahan and Serdang. From the 1860s Dutch planters turned it into a great plantation belt of tobacco, rubber and oil palm worked by imported labourers.

eastern-desert.s: The Eastern Desert is the arid, mountainous region between the Nile valley and the Red Sea, stretching from Egypt into Sudan. It held gold, copper and hard stone quarries worked since predynastic times, and routes such as the Wadi Hammamat linked the Nile to the Red Sea.

edward-hyde-governor.s: Edward Hyde was an English colonial official, a cousin of Queen Anne, who went to Carolina as deputy governor and in 1712 became the first governor of a separate Province of North Carolina. His brief rule was dominated by Cary's Rebellion and the Tuscarora War.

edward-iii-of-england.s: Edward III of England reigned from 1327 to 1377. Claiming the French crown, he began the Hundred Years' War, won the battles of Sluys and Crécy, and took Calais after a long siege in 1346–1347.

eitel-frederick-iv-count-of-hohenzollern.n: Eitel Frederick IV, Count of Hohenzollern-Hechingen
eitel-frederick-iv-count-of-hohenzollern.s: Eitel Frederick IV was the first Count of Hohenzollern-Hechingen, receiving the ancestral Hohenzollern castle and the town of Hechingen in the 1576 division of the County of Hohenzollern among the sons of Charles I. A patron of music and building, he made Hechingen a small…

el-dorado.s: El Dorado, 'the golden one', was a Spanish legend of a native ruler covered in gold dust, which grew into the myth of a golden city or kingdom in the interior of South America. It arose from the Muisca rite at Lake Guatavita in which a new chief offered gold to the waters.

elihan-tore.s: Elihan Töre was an Uzbek Muslim cleric from Tokmok who became president of the Second East Turkestan Republic, proclaimed at Ghulja in northern Xinjiang in November 1944. He gave the Soviet-backed rising a religious and nationalist voice.

emain-macha.s: Emain Macha, now Navan Fort near Armagh in Northern Ireland, was the legendary royal centre of the Ulaid and the seat of King Conchobar in the Ulster Cycle. Excavations revealed a huge timber building of about 95 BCE, filled with stones and burned.

emerita-augusta.s: Emerita Augusta, modern Mérida in Spain, was a Roman colony founded in 25 BCE for veterans of the Cantabrian Wars. It became the capital of Lusitania and later the seat of the vicarius of the Diocese of Hispania, with a theatre, amphitheatre, aqueducts and a long bridge over…

emilio-castelar.s: Emilio Castelar was a Spanish historian, orator and republican politician who drafted the federal constitution of 1873 and was the fourth and last president of the executive power of the First Spanish Republic, from September 1873 to January 1874. He ruled by decree to fight…

emperor-guangwu-of-han.s: Emperor Guangwu of Han, born Liu Xiu, was a descendant of the Han imperial house who rose against Wang Mang's Xin dynasty and restored the Han in 25 CE, founding the Eastern Han with its capital at Luoyang. He reunified China by 36, conquering the Chengjia state in Sichuan,…

emperor-xiaojing-of-eastern-wei.s: Emperor Xiaojing of Eastern Wei, born Yuan Shanjian, was the only emperor of the Eastern Wei. The general Gao Huan placed him on the throne as a boy in 534 and moved the court to Ye.

eric-bloodaxe.s: Eric Bloodaxe was a son of Harald Fairhair who ruled Norway briefly in the 930s before being driven out by his brother Haakon. He later ruled the Viking Kingdom of York twice, around 947–948 and 952–954.

eric-gairy.s: Eric Gairy was a Grenadian trade unionist and politician who led the labour unrest of 1951 and founded the Grenada United Labour Party. He became chief minister, then premier, and led Grenada to independence in 1974 as its first prime minister.

eric-the-victorious.s: Eric the Victorious was a king of the Swedes around Uppsala in the late 10th century, the first Swedish king known with reasonable certainty. He won his name by defeating his nephew Styrbjörn the Strong at Fýrisvellir near Uppsala in the 980s.

ernest-casimir-i-count-of-nassau-dietz.n: Ernest Casimir I, Count of Nassau-Dietz
ernest-casimir-i-count-of-nassau-dietz.s: Ernest Casimir I was a son of John VI of Nassau-Dillenburg who received Diez in the 1606 partition and founded the Nassau-Dietz line. A general of the Dutch Republic, he became stadtholder of Friesland, Groningen and Drenthe and was killed at the siege of Roermond in 1632.

etienne-de-flacourt.s: Étienne de Flacourt was a French colonial governor of Fort-Dauphin in south-eastern Madagascar for the French East India Company from 1648 to 1655. His History of the Great Island of Madagascar of 1658 described the island's peoples, especially the Antanosy, its plants and…

european-communities.s: The European Communities were three organisations founded by Belgium, France, West Germany, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands: the European Coal and Steel Community of 1951, and the European Economic Community and Euratom of 1957. They shared institutions from 1967,…

emperor-wenxuan-of-northern-qi.s: Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi, born Gao Yang, was a son of the general Gao Huan, who had dominated the Eastern Wei. In 550 he forced Emperor Xiaojing to abdicate and founded the Northern Qi dynasty with its capital at Ye.

emperor-wu-of-liang.s: Emperor Wu of Liang, born Xiao Yan, founded the Liang dynasty in southern China and reigned from 502 to 549. A kinsman of the Southern Qi imperial house and one of the Eight Friends of Jingling, he rebelled against Xiao Baojuan in 501 and took Jiankang.

engelbert-dollfuss.s: Engelbert Dollfuss was an Austrian Christian Social politician, chancellor from 1932. In March 1933 he suspended parliament and ruled by decree, banning the Communists and Austrian Nazis.

eberhard-i-duke-of-wurttemberg.s: Eberhard I, Duke of Württemberg, called the Bearded (im Bart), was count of Württemberg-Urach from 1459 as Eberhard V. He founded the University of Tübingen in 1477 and reunited the divided county by the Treaty of Münsingen in 1482.

eannatum.s: Eannatum was a king of the Sumerian city-state of Lagash around 2450 BCE. He defeated Umma in a long border war, commemorated on the Stele of the Vultures, and campaigned against Kish, Akshak, Mari and Elam.

early-le-dynasty.s: The Early Lê dynasty ruled Đại Cồ Việt, in northern Vietnam, from 980 to 1009. Its founder Lê Hoàn took power from the Đinh dynasty as a Song invasion loomed and defeated the Song in 981, also campaigning against Champa.

early-minoan-period.s: The Early Minoan period is the first phase of the Bronze Age Minoan civilisation of Crete, from about 3100 to 2100 BCE. Villages grew into larger settlements, with communal tombs, fine pottery and metalwork, and trade links across the Aegean.

east-bengal.s: East Bengal was the name of the eastern province of Pakistan from partition in 1947 until 1955, formed from the Muslim-majority eastern part of Bengal and the Sylhet district of Assam. Separated from West Pakistan by India, it held most of the country's population.

east-karelia.s: East Karelia is the part of Karelia that lay under Russian rule, east of the Finnish border, between Lake Ladoga, Lake Onega and the White Sea. Much of the Kalevala folk poetry was collected among its Karelian villages.

east-pakistan.s: East Pakistan was the eastern wing of Pakistan from 1955, when East Bengal was renamed, until 1971. Though it held most of Pakistan's population, its people resented political and economic domination by West Pakistan.

eastern-settlement.s: The Eastern Settlement was the larger of the two Norse colonies in Greenland, founded around 985 by settlers led by Erik the Red near modern Qaqortoq. It had farms, churches and a bishop's seat at Garðar.

ebiri-moro.s: Ebiri Moro was a king of Aowin, an Akan state in the forest of the western Gold Coast. In the early 18th century, during a succession crisis in Asante, his forces raided the Asante capital Kumasi.

edmund-albanach-de-burgh.s: Edmund Albanach de Burgh was the founder of the Mac William Iochtar lordship in north Connacht. After the murder of the 3rd Earl of Ulster in 1333, he seized the de Burgh lands in Mayo and adopted the Gaelic title Mac William Iochtar, the Lower Mac William.

edmund-andros.s: Edmund Andros was an English colonial administrator who governed New York from 1674 to 1681. In 1686 he became governor of the Dominion of New England, which merged the northern colonies under royal rule without elected assemblies.

edmund-barton.s: Edmund Barton was an Australian lawyer and politician who led the federation movement in the 1890s. He became the first prime minister of the Commonwealth of Australia in 1901, when Parliament met in Melbourne, and his government passed the Immigration Restriction Act.

edmund-pnischeck.s: Edmund Pnischeck was mayor of Lorch on the Rhine and head of the improvised administration of the Free State Bottleneck, the strip of land left unoccupied between the Allied bridgeheads at Koblenz and Mainz from 1919 to 1923. Cut off from the rest of Germany, his…

edo-wiemken-the-elder.s: Edo Wiemken the Elder was a Frisian chieftain active from about 1359 who built Jever, together with Rüstringen and Östringen, into a lordship. He allied at times with pirates such as the Victual Brothers.

edouard-hesling.s: Édouard Hesling was a French colonial administrator and the first governor of Upper Volta, created in 1919 from part of French Sudan with its capital at Ouagadougou. Governing until 1927, he relied on forced labour to build roads and administrative buildings and to promote…

edward-byllynge.s: Edward Byllynge was an English Quaker who in 1674, with John Fenwick, bought Lord Berkeley's half of New Jersey. Heavily in debt, he placed his share in the hands of trustees including William Penn, who drew up the liberal Concessions and Agreements of 1677 for the colony of…

edward-cornwallis.s: Edward Cornwallis was a British army officer and governor of Nova Scotia from 1749 to 1752. In 1749 he founded Halifax as a naval base and new capital with about 2,500 settlers.

edward-hewett.s: Edward Hewett was a British naval officer and consul for the Bights of Benin and Biafra. In 1884, ahead of the Berlin Conference, he signed treaties of protection with rulers of the Niger delta states, allowing Britain to proclaim the Oil Rivers Protectorate in June 1885, the…

edward-seaga.s: Edward Seaga was a Jamaican politician and leader of the Jamaica Labour Party who served as prime minister from 1980 to 1989. He came to power after an election marked by about 800 political killings, ending Michael Manley's socialist government.

edward-vernon.s: Edward Vernon was a British admiral in the War of Jenkins' Ear. He captured Portobelo with six ships in 1739, a success celebrated across Britain, but his great assault on Cartagena de Indias in 1741 failed against the defences led by Blas de Lezo and Viceroy Sebastián de Eslava.

edward-warner.s: Edward Warner was an English colonist, son of Sir Thomas Warner, the founder of the colony of Saint Kitts. In 1632 he led settlers from Saint Kitts to found the English colony of Antigua and served as its first governor.

edwin-of-northumbria.s: Edwin of Northumbria was king of Deira and Bernicia from 616 and the most powerful ruler in England of his day. Around 617 he seized the British kingdom of Elmet and expelled its king Ceretic.

edwin-von-manteuffel.s: Edwin von Manteuffel was a Prussian field marshal who commanded armies in the wars of 1866 and 1870–1871 and led the German occupation forces in France until 1873. In 1879 he became the first imperial governor (Statthalter) of Alsace-Lorraine in Strasbourg, where he tried,…

ehsan-khan-kangarlu.s: Ehsan Khan Kangarlu was a member of the Kangarlu dynasty of the Nakhichevan Khanate and the last of its khans. During the Russo-Persian War of 1826–1828 he went over to the Russians and surrendered the fortress of Abbasabad, and after the Treaty of Turkmenchay ceded…

ehsanollah-khan-dustdar.s: Ehsanollah Khan Dustdar was an Iranian revolutionary who led the radical left wing of the Jangali movement in Gilan. In 1920 he joined Mirza Kuchik Khan in the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic, then helped push Kuchik Khan aside in a coup with the Communist Party of Iran.

elbe-germanic-peoples.s: The Elbe Germanic peoples are a group of early Germanic peoples defined by archaeologists and historians in the Elbe basin, broadly matching the Irminones of Roman writers. They included Suebian peoples such as the Semnones, Hermunduri and Marcomanni.

elisa-bonaparte.s: Elisa Bonaparte, Napoleon's eldest surviving sister, was made Princess of Lucca and Piombino in 1805 and ruled it with energy, reforming its administration and promoting the marble industry of Massa and Carrara, which was added to her lands. From 1809 she was also Grand…

elizabeth-i.s: Elizabeth I was Queen of England and Ireland from 1558 to 1603, the last Tudor monarch. Her religious settlement established the Church of England, and her reign saw the defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588, early English overseas ventures and a flowering of literature.

elizabeth-ii.s: Elizabeth II was Queen of the United Kingdom from 1952 to 2022, the longest reign of any British monarch. During her reign most of Britain's colonies became independent; several, including Tanganyika in 1961, first kept her as head of state.

ellen-johnson-sirleaf.s: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is a Liberian economist and politician who was elected president in 2005, the first elected woman head of state in Africa. Taking office in 2006 after the civil wars, she led reconstruction, debt relief and the response to the Ebola epidemic of 2014.

ellice-islands.s: The Ellice Islands are a chain of atolls in the central Pacific, today the state of Tuvalu. Britain declared a protectorate over them in 1892, together with the Gilbert Islands, and they formed part of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony from 1916.

elmina-note.s: The Elmina Note was a document entitling an African power to a regular rent paid by the Dutch for the land of their castle at Elmina on the Gold Coast. Held at first by Denkyira, it passed to the Ashanti Empire after its victory over Denkyira in 1701.

elwell-otis.s: Elwell Otis was a United States Army general who served as military governor of the Philippines from 1898 to 1900. He commanded American forces at the outbreak of the Philippine–American War in 1899 and repeatedly claimed the insurgency was nearly over.

emile-ollivier.s: Émile Ollivier was a French liberal politician who rallied to Napoleon III and in January 1870 became head of government of the parliamentary 'Liberal Empire'. His ministry was approved by a plebiscite in May 1870, but he led France into the Franco-Prussian War that July, and…

emmanuel-endeley.s: Emmanuel Endeley was a Cameroonian physician and politician who led the Southern Cameroons in British Cameroons. He headed the territory's government from 1954 and became its first premier in 1958, favouring close ties with Nigeria.

emmanuel-macron.s: Emmanuel Macron is a French politician who was elected President of the French Fifth Republic in 2017 at the age of 39, having founded the centrist movement En Marche the year before. He was re-elected in 2022.

emmanuel-philibert-duke-of-savoy.s: Emmanuel Philibert, Duke of Savoy, won fame as a general for Spain, defeating the French at St Quentin in 1557. The Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis in 1559 restored his duchy, occupied by France, and he moved the capital from Chambéry to Turin.

emomali-rahmon.s: Emomali Rahmon is a Tajik politician from Kulob who became head of state of Tajikistan in 1992, during the civil war, and president in 1994. A peace agreement with the United Tajik Opposition ended the war in 1997.

emperor-an-of-jin.s: Emperor An of Jin, Sima Dezong, reigned over the Eastern Jin dynasty from 396 to 419 but was severely disabled and never ruled himself. In 403 the warlord Huan Xuan forced him to abdicate and proclaimed his own state of Chu.

emperor-gaozong-of-tang.s: Emperor Gaozong of Tang, Li Zhi, reigned from 649 to 683 and saw Tang power reach its greatest extent with victories over the Western Turks and the conquest of Goguryeo in 668. In 655 he made Wu Zhao his empress, and as he became ill she took over government, later founding…

emperor-gaozong-of-song.s: Emperor Gaozong of Song, Zhao Gou, a son of Emperor Huizong, escaped the Jurchen capture of Kaifeng in 1127 and was enthroned as the first emperor of the Southern Song. He established the capital at Lin'an (Hangzhou) and in 1141 made peace with the Jin, executing the general…

emperor-go-daigo.s: Emperor Go-Daigo of Japan reigned from 1318 and plotted to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate. Exiled to the Oki islands, he escaped, and in 1333 his supporters destroyed the Hōjō regime, opening the Kenmu Restoration of direct imperial rule.

emperor-ming-of-liu-song.s: Emperor Ming of Liu Song, Liu Yu, took the throne in 466 after the murder of his nephew Liu Ziye. His reign was marked by the slaughter of many of his own relatives and by the loss of the lands north of the Huai river to Northern Wei, which weakened the Liu Song dynasty.

emperor-ming-of-southern-qi.s: Emperor Ming of Southern Qi, Xiao Luan, was a nephew of the dynasty's founder who seized the throne in 494 after deposing and killing two young emperors. Fearing rivals, he had large numbers of the founder's descendants and other princes put to death.

emperor-mingzong-of-later-tang.s: Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang, Li Siyuan, was a Shatuo general and adopted son of Li Keyong who took the throne in 926 after the death of Emperor Zhuangzong. His reign restored a measure of order to northern China, and under his minister Feng Dao work began in 932 on the…

emperor-shizong-of-jin.s: Emperor Shizong of Jin, Wanyan Yong, reigned over the Jurchen Jin dynasty from 1161 to 1189 after the overthrow of Prince Hailing. He made peace with the Southern Song in 1165 and promoted Jurchen language and traditions while Confucian learning flourished.

emperor-shun-of-liu-song.s: Emperor Shun of Liu Song, Liu Zhun, was the last emperor of the Liu Song dynasty, placed on the throne as a child in 477 by the general Xiao Daocheng. In 479 Xiao forced him to abdicate and founded the Southern Qi dynasty, and the boy was killed soon afterwards.

emperor-taiwu-of-northern-wei.s: Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei, Tuoba Tao, reigned from 423 to 452. He defeated the Rouran and conquered Xia, Northern Yan and finally Northern Liang in 439, unifying northern China.

emperor-wen-of-western-wei.s: Emperor Wen of Western Wei, Yuan Baoju, was installed as emperor in 535 by the general Yuwen Tai after the poisoning of Emperor Xiaowu, becoming the first ruler of the Western Wei dynasty. Real power lay with Yuwen Tai throughout his reign, which ended with his death in 551.

emperor-xian-of-han.s: Emperor Xian of Han, Liu Xie, was the last emperor of the Eastern Han dynasty, reigning from 189 to 220. A puppet of successive warlords, he came under the control of Cao Cao in 196, who ruled northern China in his name.

emperor-xiaowen-of-northern-wei.s: Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei reigned from 471 to 499, at first under the regency of Empress Dowager Feng. Ruling alone from 490, he moved the capital from Pingcheng to Luoyang in 494, banned Xianbei dress and language at court and changed the imperial surname from Tuoba to…

emperor-xuan-of-northern-zhou.s: Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou, Yuwen Yun, succeeded his father Emperor Wu in 578 and ruled erratically, punishing officials harshly. He passed the throne to his young son in 579 while keeping power, and died in 580.

emperor-xuan-of-chen.s: Emperor Xuan of Chen, Chen Xu, reigned over the Chen dynasty in southern China from 569 to 582 after deposing his nephew. In 573 his armies recovered the Huai river region from Northern Qi, but Northern Zhou retook it by 579.

emperor-yuan-of-liang.s: Emperor Yuan of Liang, Xiao Yi, a son of Emperor Wu of Liang and a noted scholar, crushed the rebel Hou Jing and took the throne at Jiangling in 552. In 554 Western Wei armies captured Jiangling; the emperor burned the imperial library and was killed, and Western Wei installed…

emperor-zhaozong-of-tang.s: Emperor Zhaozong of Tang reigned from 888 to 904 as the dynasty collapsed among rival warlords. Li Maozhen, Prince of Qi, held him at Fengxiang until Zhu Wen's siege forced his handover in 903.

empress-dowager-feng.s: Empress Dowager Feng, a granddaughter of a Northern Yan ruler, was the empress of Northern Wei's Emperor Wencheng and acted as regent for Emperor Xiaowen. She dominated the court from the 470s until her death, introducing the equal-field system of land allotment in 485 and…

enabling-act-of-1933.s: The Enabling Act of 1933 was a law passed by the German Reichstag on 23 March 1933 that allowed Adolf Hitler's government to issue laws without parliament's approval, even ones departing from the constitution. Passed under intimidation after the Reichstag Fire Decree, it gave…

engke-temur.s: Engke Temür was a Chagatayid prince of Kara Del, the Mongol principality centred on Hami in the eastern Tarim region. In 1404 the Ming Empire recognised him as Prince of Zhongshun, and soon afterwards it set up the Hami Guard, making the oasis a Ming frontier client on the…

enrico-dandolo.s: Enrico Dandolo was Doge of Venice from 1192, elected in old age and nearly blind. He led the Venetian part of the Fourth Crusade, diverting it to Zara and then Constantinople, which the crusaders sacked in 1204.

enrico-de-nicola.s: Enrico De Nicola was a Neapolitan jurist and liberal politician who became provisional head of state after Italians voted to abolish the monarchy in June 1946. When the new constitution came into force on 1 January 1948 he became the first President of the Italian Republic,…

eoganacht-chaisil.s: Eóganacht Chaisil was the leading branch of the Eóganachta, the dynasty claiming descent from the legendary Eógan Mór that dominated the kingship of Munster from about the 5th century to the 10th. Its kings ruled from the Rock of Cashel in present-day County Tipperary.

epaminondas.s: Epaminondas was a Theban general and statesman who, with Pelopidas, made Thebes the leading power of Greece. His deep, left-weighted phalanx defeated Sparta at Leuctra in 371 BCE.

erdeni-batur.s: Erdeni Batur was the leader of the Choros Oirats who united the Oirat tribes in the 1630s and is regarded as the founder of the Dzungar Khanate. He took the title khong tayiji, encouraged farming and building, and in 1640 joined Khalkha and Oirat princes in drawing up the…

eric-of-friuli.s: Eric of Friuli was the Frankish duke of Friuli under Charlemagne, commanding the march that faced the Avars and the Slavs. In 796 his forces stormed the Ring, the fortified headquarters of the Avar khagan, and carried its treasure to Aachen, a blow from which the Avar…

eric-xiv-of-sweden.s: Eric XIV of Sweden, eldest son of Gustav Vasa, was king from 1560 to 1568. In 1561 Reval and the knighthoods of northern Estonia submitted to him, beginning Swedish rule there and drawing Sweden into the Livonian War.

erich-ludendorff.s: Erich Ludendorff was a German general who served as chief of staff to Paul von Hindenburg on the Eastern Front from 1914, sharing in the victory at Tannenberg. Their command, Ober Ost, ran the occupied Baltic and Belarusian lands as a military state.

erich-zeigner.s: Erich Zeigner was a Social Democratic lawyer who became minister-president of the Free State of Saxony in 1923. In October that year he took Communists into his government, and the Reich government under Gustav Stresemann sent troops into Saxony and removed him by decree.

erik-the-red.s: Erik the Red was a Norse explorer who, outlawed from Iceland for killings, explored the coast of Greenland and around 985 led settlers there, founding the Eastern Settlement near modern Qaqortoq. He farmed at Brattahlíð and was the leading chieftain of Norse Greenland.

ernest-duke-of-saxe-hildburghausen.s: Ernest, Duke of Saxe-Hildburghausen, was the sixth son of Ernest the Pious of Saxe-Gotha. In the partition of his father's inheritance in 1680 he received Hildburghausen in southern Thuringia, made the small town his residence and founded the line of Saxe-Hildburghausen.

ernest-louis-grand-duke-of-hesse.n: Ernest Louis, Grand Duke of Hesse
ernest-louis-grand-duke-of-hesse.s: Ernest Louis, Grand Duke of Hesse, reigned from 1892 to 1918 and was the last ruler of the Grand Duchy of Hesse. A grandson of Queen Victoria and brother of Empress Alexandra of Russia, he was a keen patron of the arts and in 1899 founded the Darmstadt Artists' Colony on the…

ernest-roume.s: Ernest Roume was a French colonial administrator who served as governor-general of French West Africa from 1902 to 1908. Based at Dakar, he reorganised the federation in 1904, giving the governor-general control of a common budget funded by customs revenue, and used it to…

ernesto-geisel.s: Ernesto Geisel was a Brazilian army general who served as president from 1974 to 1979, the fourth of the military dictatorship. He began a slow, controlled political opening, the distensão, eased censorship and in 1978 revoked the repressive Institutional Act Number Five.

ernst-bogislaw-von-croy.s: Ernst Bogislaw von Croÿ was a grandson of Duke Bogislaw XIII of Pomerania and the last Lutheran bishop of Cammin. After the Peace of Westphalia assigned the see to Brandenburg, he handed it over, and in 1650 it became the secular Principality of Cammin.

ernst-johann-von-biron.s: Ernst Johann von Biron was a Courland nobleman who became the favourite of Empress Anna of Russia and, with her backing, Duke of Courland and Semigallia in 1737. He commissioned Rastrelli to build Rundāle and Jelgava palaces.

ernst-toller.s: Ernst Toller was a German expressionist playwright and pacifist who led the first council government of the Bavarian Soviet Republic in April 1919 and then commanded part of its Red Army. After its fall he was sentenced to five years in prison, where he wrote plays such as…

eshmunazar-ii.s: Eshmunazar II was a Phoenician king of Sidon in the Achaemenid period, probably in the late 6th or early 5th century BCE. He is known from his black stone sarcophagus, found near Sidon in 1855 and now in the Louvre, whose long inscription curses grave robbers and records that…

essad-pasha-toptani.s: Essad Pasha Toptani was an Ottoman general and Albanian landowner who surrendered Shkodër to Montenegro in 1913 and then set up a rival government in Durrës, the Republic of Central Albania. He served Prince Wilhelm of Wied before being exiled for intrigue in 1914, returned to…

estacio-de-sa.s: Estácio de Sá was a Portuguese soldier, nephew of the governor-general Mem de Sá, who founded the city of São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro on 1 March 1565 at the foot of Sugarloaf Mountain. With Temiminó allies he fought to drive the French and their Tupinambá allies from…

estanislao-figueras.s: Estanislao Figueras was a Catalan lawyer and republican politician who became the first President of the Executive Power of the First Spanish Republic when it was proclaimed in February 1873 after Amadeo I abdicated. Overwhelmed by divisions between federal and unitary…

etienne-regnault.s: Étienne Regnault was the first commandant of Île Bourbon, now Réunion, sent by the French East India Company in 1665 with a small group of colonists. Their settlement at Saint-Paul began the island's permanent population, later joined by survivors from Fort-Dauphin on Madagascar.

ettore-tibaldi.s: Ettore Tibaldi was an Italian physician and socialist who presided over the provisional government junta of the partisan Republic of Ossola in September and October 1944. Having returned from exile in Switzerland, he led a junta of anti-Fascist parties that reorganised local…

eugen-levine.s: Eugen Leviné was a Russian-born German Communist who took over the Bavarian Soviet Republic in April 1919, a week after its proclamation, and formed a Red Army. His government decreed the socialisation of banks and industry before government troops and Freikorps crushed it in…

eugenia-charles.s: Eugenia Charles was a Dominican lawyer and leader of the Dominica Freedom Party who served as prime minister from 1980 to 1995, the first woman to head a government in the Caribbean. She survived coup plots in 1981 and, as chair of the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States,…

eugeniusz-okon.s: Eugeniusz Okoń was a radical Polish Catholic priest who, with the peasant activist Tomasz Dąbal, led the short-lived Republic of Tarnobrzeg in November 1918. As Austrian rule in Galicia collapsed, he called on peasants and returning soldiers to seize power and demanded land…

european-economic-area.s: The European Economic Area is an agreement that came into force in 1994, extending the European Union's single market to member states of the European Free Trade Association. Iceland, Norway and, from 1995, Liechtenstein take part, adopting most EU single-market law without…

evelyn-wever-croes.s: Evelyn Wever-Croes is an Aruban lawyer and politician of the People's Electoral Movement who became Prime Minister of Aruba in 2017, the first woman to hold the office. Her governments steered the island, a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, through the…

evo-morales.s: Evo Morales is a Bolivian coca growers' leader of Aymara origin who became the country's first indigenous president in 2006. Leading the Movement for Socialism, he nationalised the gas industry, cut poverty and introduced the 2009 constitution that renamed the country the…

eweka-ii.s: Eweka II was Oba of Benin from 1914 to 1933, the son of Ovonramwen, who had been exiled after the British conquest of 1897. The British allowed him to succeed as head of the Benin Native Authority, restoring the monarchy within colonial Nigeria.

ewuare-ii.s: Ewuare II is the Oba of Benin, crowned in 2016 in succession to his father Erediauwa. Before his accession he was a Nigerian diplomat, serving as ambassador to several countries.

eze-nri.s: Eze Nri was the title of the priest-king of Nri, an Igbo sacred kingdom in south-eastern Nigeria. The Eze Nri held ritual rather than military authority: his agents travelled widely to cleanse abominations, settle disputes, crown titled men and bless the yam harvest.

edmund-the-martyr.s: Edmund the Martyr was king of East Anglia until 869, when he was killed by the Great Heathen Army of the Danes. Later accounts say he was shot with arrows and beheaded for refusing to renounce Christianity.

emperor-yi-of-chu.s: Emperor Yi of Chu, born Xiong Xin, was a grandson of the earlier King Huai of Chu whom rebels against the Qin dynasty enthroned in 208 BCE under the same title, King Huai of Chu, as the figurehead of their rising. After the fall of Qin, Xiang Yu gave him the empty title of…

ecumenical-patriarch-of-constantinople.s: The Patriarch of Constantinople, styled Ecumenical Patriarch, is the archbishop of Constantinople and senior bishop of the Eastern Orthodox Church. The patriarch oversaw churches across the Byzantine world and, under Ottoman rule, led the Orthodox community of the empire.

east-african-rift.s: The East African Rift is a system of rift valleys running from the Afar region of Ethiopia through Kenya to Mozambique, part of what is often called the Great Rift Valley. Its floor holds a chain of lakes and fertile volcanic soils.

emperor-wu-of-jin.s: Emperor Wu of Jin, born Sima Yan, was the founder of the Western Jin dynasty. In 266 he forced the last Cao Wei emperor to abdicate, and in 280 he conquered Eastern Wu, briefly reuniting China after the Three Kingdoms period.

emperor-daowu-of-northern-wei.s: Tuoba Gui, posthumously Emperor Daowu, was the founder of the Northern Wei dynasty. A grandson of Tuoba Shiyijian, he restored the Tuoba state of Dai in 386 after the collapse of Former Qin and soon renamed it Wei.

empedocles.s: Empedocles was a Greek philosopher, poet and statesman from Acragas in Sicily. In his poems he taught that all things are made of four roots, earth, water, air and fire, mixed and separated by the forces of Love and Strife, an idea that shaped the later theory of the four…

edgar-james-banks.s: Edgar James Banks was an American archaeologist, diplomat and antiquities dealer. From 1903 to 1905 he led the University of Chicago's excavations at Bismaya, the site of the Sumerian city of Adab, recovering temple remains, statues and inscribed tablets.

el-djem.s: El Djem is a town in eastern Tunisia on the site of the Roman city of Thysdrus, which grew rich on olive oil. In 238 a revolt there proclaimed Gordian I emperor.

ellac.s: Ellac was the eldest son of Attila. Around 448 Attila made him king over the Akatziri, a people north of the Black Sea.

essaouira.s: Essaouira, known to Europeans as Mogador, is a port city on the Atlantic coast of Morocco. Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah founded the present town in 1760 as a royal trading port, laid out by the French engineer Théodore Cornut within strong sea walls.

edi-rama.s: Edi Rama is an Albanian politician and painter who has led the Socialist Party since 2005 and became prime minister in 2013. As mayor of Tirana from 2000 to 2011 he became known for having the capital's drab buildings painted in bright colours.

enver-hoxha.s: Enver Hoxha was the communist ruler of Albania from 1944 until his death in 1985. A founder and first secretary of the Albanian Communist Party in 1941, he led the Partisans to victory in 1944 and built a Stalinist dictatorship.

eran.s: Eran is an archaeological site in the Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh, central India, the ancient town of Airikina. It holds important Gupta-era monuments, including a pillar of Budhagupta and a colossal stone boar of Vishnu's Varaha incarnation inscribed in the first year of…

el-camino-real-california.s: El Camino Real ('the Royal Road') was the route linking the 21 Spanish missions of Alta California, together with its presidios and pueblos, from San Diego to Sonoma. It developed from 1769 as Franciscan missionaries and soldiers moved north along the coast.

este-veneto.s: Este is a town in the province of Padua, north-eastern Italy, at the foot of the Euganean Hills. As Ateste it was a leading centre of the ancient Veneti, giving its name to the Este culture of the Iron Age, and its museum holds rich finds of bronze situlae and Venetic…
